title: Predictive bucketized pricing notes
content:
Goal: sketch a compact, predictive bucketized credits model that maps to real unit costs and gives customers predictable monthly bills while preserving cost signals for high-throughput interactive apps.

Context / motivation:
- We get lots of asks for simpler monthly invoices rather than per-token spikes.
- Simple tiers hide cost signals and can be gamed; pure pay-as-you-go is accurate but noisy and scares customers with variance.
- A hybrid: bucketed upfront credits that replenish monthly + small payg overage (or top-up) seems promising. Need back-of-envelope unit economics to test feasibility.

Assumptions (ballpark -- replace with infra numbers):
- Infra cost per inference token (decoded+compute amortized): $0.000006 per token (6e-6) for our mid-tier models when utilizing batching and caching.
- API overhead / request routing / storage / control plane: $0.000002 per token equivalent.
- Customer acquisition and support allocation per active paying account (S&M + CS amortized): $20/mo (target).
- Desired gross margin (hosted) target: 60%+ at scale.
- Typical interactive session: 1 user convo/day => 4000 tokens/day => 120k tokens/mo. But different personas below.

Design primitives to play with:
- Buckets: monthly credit allotment purchased upfront (discounted vs PAYG).
- Velocity bands (low/med/high concurrency) adjust recommended bucket for SLA/cost.
- Overage: PAYG price or auto-topup credit pack; could be higher than bucket unit price to encourage reasonable sizing.
- Carryover: allow small rollover (e.g., 10% unused) to reduce churn complaints.
- Commitment discounts: bigger commits => lower per-token price (reflects reserved capacity).

Price math framework (simple):
- Base PAYG list price for customers (public): $0.000012 / token (2x infra cost as initial margin target).
- Bucket unit price = PAYG * (1 - bucket_discount). For example 20% discount -> $0.0000096/token.
- Effective gross margin = (bucket_price - infra_cost) / bucket_price. Need to include per-account CAC/S&M amortization (convert to $/token by dividing monthly fixed by expected tokens used).

Profiles (3 personas) with quick calcs:
1) Light tool: "Notetaker"
   - Usage: 10k tokens/mo (low).
   - PAYG cost to customer @ $0.000012 = $0.12/mo.
   - If we force a minimum monthly (bucket) ~$5 -> this obviously doesn't fit. So we need micro-buckets for hobbyists e.g., 5k credits for $1/mo.
   - Micro-bucket example: 5k tokens for $0.60 (50% of PAYG list) -> per-token $0.00012? Wait re-check: 0.60/5000 = $0.00012, that's much higher than list. So micro-buckets need a different structure: maybe per-interaction credits (sessions) rather than pure tokens.
   - Conclusion: we must keep a true PAYG for ultra-light users or offer a very cheap starter pack with limited features (no streaming / rate-limit).

2) Mid usage: "Productivity app"
   - Usage: 120k tokens/mo (approx 1 conv/day per active user).
   - PAYG cost = 120k * $0.000012 = $1.44/mo. (Customer sees low cost; S&M dominates.)
   - If we propose a monthly bucket of 150k credits at 20% discount: bucket price = 150k * $0.0000096 = $1.44 (same ballpark). With S&M $20/mo allocated, break-even becomes tricky.
   - Realistic: for SMBs we expect multiple seats; price per-account should include seat/feature component. So bucket alone can't carry S&M. Suggest: combine bucket for tokens + per-seat base fee ($5-15/mo).

3) Heavy usage: "Conversational SaaS (prod)"
   - Usage: 25M tokens/mo (POC->prod scale for chat app).
   - PAYG cost to customer = 25M * $0.000012 = $300/mo.
   - Infra cost = 25M * $0.000006 = $150/mo. CP/ops = 25M * $0.000002 = $50/mo. Total cost = $200/mo. If we sell bucket at 20% discount: revenue = 25M * $0.0000096 = $240/mo -> negative gross margin if we forget S&M. Wait math: revenue $240 - infra+cp $200 = $40 gross profit (16.7%), far below target 60%. So to hit 60%, bucket price must be ~5x current infra cost.
   - Another lever: Reserved capacity (dedicated) customers get significantly lower infra cost (say $0.000002/token) and we sign annual commitments. So bucket model should be targeted at hosted API customers; large workloads should be nudged to Dedicated.

Implications from the quick numbers:
- Per-account fixed costs dominate for low-usage customers -> need cheap free tier + payg or micro-credits.
- Mid-tier with many seats: introduce per-seat base + pooled credits for team to make economics sane.
- High-volume customers: incentivize Dedicated/reserved pricing and multi-month/annual commits.

Bucket sizing heuristics (initial rules):
- Starter: 5k tokens (free tier + usage) -> keep PAYG for <50k/mo to avoid forcing bad buy.
- Developer: 150k tokens/mo + API key analytics -> $X + small per-seat fee.
- Team: 2M tokens/mo pooled -> mid discount (25%) and carryover 10%.
- Enterprise: 20M+ tokens/mo -> negotiate reserved price + SLA.

Unit econ worked example (Team bucket)
- Bucket: 2M tokens @ bucket unit price $0.000008 (33% off PAYG) -> revenue = $16/mo. Hmm check: 2,000,000 * 0.000008 = $16. That seems too low vs S&M. Need scale: with 2M tokens our infra cost at 6e-6 = $12; cp cost $4 -> total $16 cost. So revenue equals cost -> zero margin. Conclusion: our per-token pricing needs to be significantly higher or assumptions wrong.
- If target gross margin 60%, required bucket price per token = infra_total / (1 - 0.6) = cost_per_token / 0.4. With cost_per_token = 0.000008 -> price = 0.00002. That is ~2x current PAYG list price. So current list (0.000012) doesn't get us to 60% when including CP. Need to reconcile: either lower infra cost (through batching/reserved) or accept lower margin and monetize via seat/feature fees.

Operational & UX concerns:
- Meter transparency: customers must see token burn live, estimated monthly spend.
- Auto top-up vs overage: top-up packs are simpler and cap spend surprises. Overage charged at PAYG till user turns off.
- Billing UX: show equivalent $/1k tokens and example sessions per month to make it tangible.
- Contracting: for buckets > X tokens, require card + billing admin (reduce fraud).

Open questions / to-dos:
- Get accurate infra per-token numbers across model families (small/medium/large) and per deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).
- Decide a minimum realistic bucket price that covers fixed S&M per-account for mid-tier (or move S&M to per-seat).
- Test a 3-month rolling commit discount vs monthly to incent predictability without full annual lock.
- Consider hybrid unit: mix tokens + session credits (session credit maps to average prompt/response pair to better price interactive apps).

Notes to self: this is a scratchpad, not a proposal. Next step: convert to a simple spreadsheet with variable knobs: infra_cost_per_token, cp_cost_per_token, bucket_discount, per-seat fee, expected tokens per seat to model revenue and margin across cohort sizes. Then run sensitivity for infra_cost +/-30%.

Slack refs: #pricing, #customer-obs for recent asks.

Rough conclusion: bucket model can be viable for mid and high usage if we (A) ensure per-token price covers infra+cp+target margin given realistic batching, or (B) carve out per-account/seat fees to cover fixed costs and keep bucket price nearer to infra. For very small users, preserve true PAYG or cheap micro-packs to avoid forcing high minimums.

-- end of scratchpad --
